meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at twenty to five, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so who made that decision, and when?

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. I'm writing down that you said it was wrong. Now tell me what you're basing this on, because if the answer is a percentage from a piece of software, we're done here and I'm going upstairs.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me. What is it, and what dates are on it?

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

Slide that over so I can read it myself, Hale. 11:31, 11:52, 11:58, the night before it was due; I'm writing those down. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so all this shows me is when it went into that file, and did anyone ask him where the draft came from before that zero went in?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.

"Anywhere in the history." The history of that one file, Hale, which tells you nothing about a notebook, another document, or a different computer. So I'll ask again, and I want a straight answer: did you speak to Owen before you entered that zero, yes or no?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale, that's what outlines are for. I'll want a copy of that October 15 outline, and you still haven't answered me: did you speak to Owen before the zero went in, yes or no?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

"Not in Hamlet." I'm writing that down, and I'll check it myself tonight. Whatever comes out of this, Hale, nothing goes on Owen's record and not one student in that class hears about it, and you still owe me an answer about whether you spoke to him first.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.

"What the document shows." Fine, then let's talk about what you're putting on the table, because I haven't heard a proposal yet. And that's the third time you've stepped around my question, so I'll take the silence as a no.
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.

A sample from six weeks ago, written in forty minutes with you standing over him. Show me exactly which lines you think don't match, Hale, because I'm not going to guess at your argument for you. And then tell me what you're proposing.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Section 4.4, and its mark replaces the zero. If Owen does it, it's to put this behind him, it happens privately, not in front of his class, it's graded before December 1, and I get "nothing goes on file" from you in writing. Ten minutes, Hale, so do I have that or not?
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.

Lunch, your room, nobody else there; I'm writing that down. That's one of three, and you still haven't said it'll be marked before December 1 or that I'll have "nothing goes on file" in writing. And the zero comes out of that gradebook before Owen sits down to write, not after.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

"Comfortable." I've already told you, Hale: an email from you tonight, cc the principal, saying the zero is withdrawn pending the rewrite, it's marked before December 1, and nothing goes on Owen's record. You send that, and he'll be in your room at lunch.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.

Okay. I want it by nine tonight, with the date of the rewrite in it, and if it isn't in my inbox by then I'm in the principal's office at eight tomorrow morning. And Hale, the next time you have a concern about my son, you pick up the phone before you touch that gradebook.
Is there anything else you want me to include?

I've given you my terms, Hale, and I'll check every line of that email against them. One more: you tell Owen about the rewrite yourself, privately, not through a notification on his phone. I have a call in a few minutes, so are we done?
Then I'll send it by eight.

Eight o'clock, then, and I'm holding you to it. Zero withdrawn pending the rewrite, lunch in your room, marked before December 1, nothing on Owen's record, all of it in writing, and if one piece of that is missing, I'm upstairs first thing tomorrow.
Thank you for coming in.
Eight o'clock, Hale.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Tomorrow's November 11, Hale, there's no school. Put the real date in the email.
